title: Changes across an absorption line identify the radius of a thin corotating ring with a curved log opacity pattern
abstract: We derive a radius diagnostic for a narrow, optically thin, equatorial ring that rotates rigidly and is viewed edge-on. Time and velocity derivatives of the log absorption remove any unknown positive response that is fixed in time at each velocity. The radius is locally unique when the angular log opacity has nonzero curvature. Constant and locally exponential patterns give exact failures. A changing absorption weight can make the centroid drift differ greatly from material acceleration. A reproducible fit removes the fixed velocity response and profiles the ring radius. In one correctly specified synthetic pattern at four stellar radii, 100 draws with independent log noise of standard deviation 0.03 give radius RMSE 0.0156 stellar radii. Spectral smoothing can bias this fit despite small noise errors. This is a conditional mathematical method, not a new measurement of a complex periodic variable. Finite line width, saturation, evolving emission, several radii, inclination and gas-dust differences limit its use. Original code, proofs, aggregate tests and failure cases are included.

display.caption: A synthetic resolved absorption profile, trial-radius loss curves, and the failure of centroid drift for an extended uniform ring. No observed spectrum is shown.
